extracted.intended_audience: EPA rulewriters, regulators, and stakeholders in oil & natural gas MACT/NSPS rulemaking (advocates, counsel, permitting authorities)
extracted.subtask_description: Public-comment / advocacy guidance criticizing EPA's 2011 MACT/NSPS review for oil & natural gas sources and prescribing legal, technical, and data-quality standards EPA must follow when setting MACT floors and related requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider emission reductions available from demonstrated technology
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA must not ignore the emission reductions available from this technology for many sources and should address such issues by establishing subcategories of sources that operate within the envelope of the available technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If technologies demonstrably achieve lower emissions in many sources, EPA should create subcategories rather than claim technologies are inapplicable; failure to do so is 'not lawful or reasonable.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate RBLC/BACT findings into MACT review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's RBLC review identified practices (e.g., BACT determination for dehydrator efficiency of 98 percent) that were not adequately considered; EPA may not lawfully conclude RBLC identified nothing new when it in fact did.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review RBLC entries and BACT determinations and evaluate whether they represent advances or achievable performance for MACT floors; do not dismiss RBLC results without record support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use current, representative emissions data (do not rely on outdated surveys)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA should not base MACT floors on 1997 data if newer emissions data (e.g., 2005 NEI) show different, generally improved performance; new data for small dehydrators are available and show far lower HAP emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the precedent of sending updated questionnaires when older data are outdated; use NEI and other current data sets to determine representative performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base existing-source MACT floor on the top performers in current, representative data
rubrics_metrics.description: The MACT floor nominally reflects the performance of the unit that is the top 6th percentile (average of top 12%); the floor should approximate that performance so a significant majority must take steps to comply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure MACT-floor calculations actually represent the top performers; verify that the floor would require a substantial fraction of sources to take action; correct calculation errors that make the floor approximate much worse performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure adequate sample size and representativeness when setting floors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not base MACT floors on extremely small or unrepresentative samples (e.g., when a floor is effectively based on the average of 5 units or a small, biased 1997 survey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate sample sizes, consider measurement vs. estimated data mix, and avoid setting floors from small-n results without acknowledging uncertainty and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for stack flow rates and use appropriate units (e.g., lb/MMscf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information standing alone (emission rates without stack flow) is insufficient; stack flow rate data in NEI can be used to set MACT floors and emission limits on a lb/MMscf basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set emission limits in comparable units used historically (lb/MMscf or ppm of exhaust gas) rather than inventing nonstandard normalized metrics that obscure compliance and comparability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate system-level performance, not just individual control devices
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA improperly measured performance of a single control device rather than the demonstrated performance of the whole source/system; the D.C. Circuit instructs examining system performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the entire control system (e.g., flash tank + condenser + downstream controls) when determining achievable emissions; do not normalize away benefits achieved by upstream measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid normalizing outlet limits by intake concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA proposed a new metric (grams per std m3 per ppm intake) that normalizes output by inlet concentration, which defeats identifying better performers and improperly focuses on a device rather than source emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not combine inlet concentration normalization with outlet metrics; recalculate MACT floors using current data and system-level performance measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider pollution prevention and process modifications as part of MACT review
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA improperly excluded pollution prevention/process modifications from MACT consideration asserting they were not considered under MACT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MACT reviews must consider pollution prevention and process modifications revealed in RBLC or other programs rather than dismissing them as outside MACT's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include tanks with breathing and working losses when assessing storage-vessel emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA originally limited 'facility' to tanks with potential for flash emissions and failed to justify excluding breathing and working losses; breathing and working losses are significant emission points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When developing standards for storage vessels, evaluate all significant HAP emission pathways (flashing, breathing, working, etc.) and provide rationale if any are excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not assume technologies 'were considered' without record support
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA claimed certain advances had been 'considered' in 1999 but provided no record support; rejection of developments because they 'fall within broadly defined classes' is improper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite explicit evidence showing prior consideration and analysis; if RBLC or Natural Gas Star identifies specific developments, EPA must evaluate whether they are developments relevant to MACT limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set new-source MACT floor based on actual performance of best performing source(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The new-source MACT floor should reflect the actual performance of the best performing source, not merely the regulatory limit that defined minimum acceptable performance historically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess demonstrated performance of best-in-class new sources and set the new-source floor to reflect those demonstrated emission reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not carry over NSPS cost-based exemptions into MACT without impact analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA carried over exemptions and deferred monitoring/repair options (artifacts of Part 60 NSPS that may consider cost) into MACT without evaluating impacts on emissions or public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MACT determinations may not rely on cost-justified exemptions without analyzing emission consequences; evaluate health impacts and compare to best-performing facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject blanket exemptions for components servicing streams <10% VHAP without evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA provided an exemption for components servicing streams with less than 10 percent volatile HAP content without evaluating the impact on emissions, control level, or rule effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform analysis to determine how such percentage-based exemptions affect overall emissions; do not adopt exemptions by analogy without showing equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require quantification of leak rates and impose caps on allowed emissions from unrepaired components
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal rules permit up to 2% of leaking valves to be 'unrepaired' with no cap on amount of HAP emissions; Federal rules do not require quantification of ongoing leaks or impose a cap on HAP allowed to leak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require measurement/quantification of ongoing leaks, set numeric caps on emissions from non-repaired or non-repairable components, and avoid open-ended percentage allowances without emission limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt more stringent detection limits, monitoring frequencies, and repair obligations where feasible
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed improvements (e.g., detection limits lowered for pumps from 10,000 ppm to 2,000 ppm and valves from 10,000 ppm to 500 ppm) are feasible and represent improvements over existing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider adopting detection limits and repair schedules closer to leading local programs (e.g., BAAQMD) and recent NSPS standards (Subpart VVa) while ensuring exclusions (e.g., methane exclusion) do not nullify benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include methane or account for whole-stream monitoring to detect VHAP effectively
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal rules exclude methane from monitoring, which can make a 500 ppm VHAP detection limit equivalent to 10,000 ppm when methane comprises most of the stream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either include methane in monitoring or ensure detection limits account for methane fraction so that effective VHAP detection is comparable to stringent local programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit number of components awaiting repair and require mass-emission testing for non-repairables
rubrics_metrics.description: BAAQMD requires strict limits on components awaiting repair (e.g., 0.3% valves) and mandates mass emission testing and emission limits for non-repairable components; Federal rules lack such caps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider numeric component thresholds, require mass-emission tests for non-repairables, and impose per-source emission limits (e.g., pounds/day) for non-repairable components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require modern leak-detection technologies (ultrasound, optical gas imaging) as part of MACT/new-source work practices
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA dismissed ultrasonic detection because it 'provides the magnitude of the leak, but does not quantify' it; NRDC argues both ultrasonic and optical scanning should be required in addition to traditional devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and require applicable advanced detection technologies as part of MACT floors or work practice standards, and combine technologies where they demonstrably improve detection and repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess Natural Gas STAR program practices individually rather than rejecting them as 'new' wholesale
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA painted with too broad a brush by rejecting NG STAR practices as new/unproven; some NG STAR practices are established and broadly applicable and should be considered in MACT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine NG STAR-reported measures (pressurized condensate tanks, improved VRUs, directed inspection/maintenance, dry seals, etc.) and determine whether they represent achievable performance for existing/new sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate lessons from enforcement and best-practice guideline development into regulatory design
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement investigations revealed fraud in LDAR programs and consent decrees led to improved real-world effectiveness and Best Practice Guidelines; EPA did not examine these activities in its review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use enforcement findings, consent-decree outcomes, and best-practice guidelines to address real-world implementation failures, close loopholes, and strengthen monitoring/reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and correct drafting flaws, ambiguities, and unjustified exemptions to reduce uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA did not review a number of drafting flaws and ill-considered exemptions from the past that increase uncertainty and allow loopholes without justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform a careful textual review to eliminate ambiguities, define terms (e.g., 'volatile' in VHAP), clarify alternative test procedures and 'target compounds', and remove exemptions lacking analytical support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate combined control-system configurations and actual performance where multiple controls are used
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA did not evaluate performance achieved by systems employing thermal/catalytic oxidizers alone or in combination with condensers, improperly treating these as already 'considered.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess concrete system configurations and measured outcomes (not just technology classes) to determine achievable emission reductions and whether they should inform MACT floors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not dismiss technologies because they 'do not quantify' leaks when current rules also lack quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's rationale that ultrasonic detection was not considered because it 'does not quantify the leak' is inconsistent given that neither current nor proposed LDAR quantifies leak rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that comparative magnitude information from technologies like ultrasound/OGI can meaningfully improve detection and enforcement even if absolute quantification is imperfect; integrate multiple detection methods and require follow-up quantification where needed.
